description: `holon flow` ends with exit 1 when its pre-flight readiness probe meets a network, DNS or Docker outage. sandbox_executor.preflight retries a transient UNKNOWN probe result only three times, two seconds apart, so a DNS failure, a refused or reset connection, a probe that hangs with no reply, or a stopped Docker daemon lasting more than a few seconds ends the run before any branch, checkpoint or ledger write. Nothing relaunches it, so the flow then sits idle until a person notices. In a recent outage three flows stayed idle for about 16 hours each after a 40-minute network loss.
goal: Make the pre-flight gate in sandbox_executor.cli.preflight wait out a connectivity outage instead of ending the run. When the probe result is UNKNOWN and its output or hint shows a connectivity failure (DNS resolution failure such as ENOTFOUND or EAI_AGAIN, connection refused, reset, unreachable or timed out, a probe that finished with no output, or the Docker daemon not reachable), re-run the probe with exponential back-off: 30 s doubling to a 300 s cap, and give up after 60 minutes of cumulative waiting. Log each wait with its reason and the attempt number. A probe that succeeds during the wait lets the run proceed exactly as today. Authentication, quota, expired-key, not-logged-in, model-name and missing-CLI results never wait and are returned at once. When the wait gives up, print the existing report plus one line stating how long the outage lasted, and return the failed result as today so the caller still aborts before any write. Put the classification and back-off schedule in a new module, sandbox_executor/preflight_outage.py, and call it from sandbox_executor/cli/preflight.py. Pre-flight only: stage-level outages are out of scope. Add no environment variables and no CLI flags, and change no documentation. Module line budgets are frozen: holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json and any budget-check script must not be edited, and every module you touch or create must stay within the default 200-line budget.
rationale: A short outage at pre-flight currently costs a whole flow's idle time until a person relaunches it. Waiting inside the gate, with a bounded back-off, turns the outage into its own length plus one back-off step, and leaves every non-connectivity failure exactly as fast as now.
acceptance_criteria: preflight_gate returns the OK result unchanged when the first probe succeeds, with exactly one probe call and no sleep.
A connectivity UNKNOWN followed by OK returns OK after sleeps of 30 s and 60 s (injected sleep and clock in tests), and logs each wait with its reason.

A connectivity failure that persists past 60 minutes of cumulative waiting returns the failed result, prints the existing report plus the outage duration, and never sleeps longer than the 300 s cap for one step.
Quota, 401 or expired-key, not-logged-in, model-name and missing-docker-CLI results return on the first probe with no sleep and no second probe call.

Tests classify ENOTFOUND, EAI_AGAIN, 'Could not resolve host', ECONNREFUSED, ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT, 'Network is unreachable', 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon' and a no-output timeout as connectivity, and quota or auth text as not connectivity.
--skip-preflight and HOLON_SKIP_PREFLIGHT still bypass the probe with no wait.
sandbox_executor/preflight.py, holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json, the budget-check script, docs and environment registries are unchanged in the diff.
uv run pytest on the existing preflight tests (apps/sandbox-executor/tests/test_preflight*.py) and the new test file passes, and the repository lint passes on the changed files.
